title: 前出塞·其六
titleEn: Marching to the Frontier (Earlier Series, No. 6)
author: 杜甫
intro: “To catch the bandits, first catch their king” — this poem gave Chinese a proverb still used every day. But its real point comes at the end: the purpose of war is to stop aggression, not to kill as many as possible.
analysis: 《前出塞》是杜甫写的一组九首诗，用一个出征士兵的口气来写。这是第六首。前四句像军中流行的口诀（顺口好记的话）：拉弓就要拉硬弓，用箭就要用长箭；射人先射他的马，抓贼先抓他们的头领。这四句讲的是打仗的方法，抓住关键，干脆有力，“擒贼先擒王”今天已经成了常用成语，意思是做事要先解决最关键的问题。后四句意思一转，讲打仗的道理：杀人也应该有个限度，每个国家都有自己的边界；只要能制止敌人的侵犯，何必杀伤那么多人呢？唐玄宗晚年常常为了扩张领土而发动战争，杜甫在这里委婉地表示反对。前面讲“怎么打”，后面讲“为什么打、打到什么程度”，层次清楚，见识很高。
analysisEn: “Marching to the Frontier” is a set of nine poems in which Du Fu speaks in the voice of a soldier sent to the northwest. This is the sixth. The first four lines sound like a soldiers' rhyme, short and easy to remember: if you draw a bow, draw the strongest; if you use arrows, use the longest; to shoot a man, shoot his horse first; to catch the bandits, catch their king first. It is practical advice — go for what matters most — and the last line, 擒贼先擒王, is now a common idiom meaning “tackle the key problem first.” Then the poem changes direction. Killing, too, should have its limits; every country has its own borders. As long as you can stop the invader, why kill and wound so many? In Du Fu's time, Emperor Xuanzong was waging costly wars to push the borders outward, and this is a quiet but clear protest. The first half is about how to fight; the second asks why, and how far. That turn is what makes the poem more than a war song.
background: Du Fu (712–770) is thought to have written the nine “Marching to the Frontier” poems around 751–752, when the Tang was fighting costly campaigns against Tibet in the northwest. (A later set of five is called “Later Marching to the Frontier”.)
pronunciation: 当挽强 dāng（应当），强 qiáng（硬弓）；用长 cháng；射 shè；擒 qín；有限 xiàn；侵陵 líng。
version: 采用通行版本，全诗八句，组诗共九首。“苟能制侵陵”的“侵陵”有的本子作“侵凌”，意思相同。

lines.lit: Drawing a bow, one should draw a strong one;
lines.en: If you draw a bow, draw the strongest;

lines.lit: using arrows, one should use long ones.
lines.en: if you use arrows, use the longest.

lines.lit: Shooting a man, first shoot his horse;
lines.en: To bring down the rider, first shoot his horse;

lines.lit: capturing bandits, first capture their king.
lines.en: to catch the bandits, first catch their king.

lines.lit: Killing people also has a limit;
lines.en: But killing, too, should have its limits,

lines.lit: the various states each have their own borders.
lines.en: and every nation has its borders.

lines.lit: If one can stop invasion and bullying,
lines.en: If we can stop the invader,

lines.lit: how does it lie in much killing and wounding?
lines.en: why kill and maim so many?

words.en: to go out beyond the frontier
words.note: “塞”读 sài，指边疆，现代汉语有“要塞”“塞外”。
现代汉语有“挽回”“挽救”“手挽手”。
这里指硬弓，拉起来费力，射得远。
现代汉语说“抓”“捉”；“擒贼先擒王”今天是常用成语，比喻先解决关键问题。
现代汉语说“也”；书面语还用，如“亦即”。
各个国家；现代汉语说“各国”。
古义是“如果”；现代汉语“苟”多用在“一丝不苟”“苟且”里。
侵犯欺凌；现代汉语写作“侵凌”，常说“侵犯”“侵略”。
反问词，相当于“难道”“哪里”。

imagery.name: 马
imagery.zh: “射人先射马”，马是骑兵的根本，射倒战马就抓住了关键。
imagery.en: “Shoot the horse first”: the horse is what makes a cavalryman dangerous, so bringing it down is the key.

imagery.name: 关
imagery.zh: 题目“出塞”就是走出边关；诗人认为守住国界、制止侵犯就够了，不应无限扩张。
imagery.en: “Going beyond the frontier” means marching past the border passes; the poet argues that holding the border and stopping aggression is enough — not endless conquest.
